"Air Transportation At Its Best"
U
NITED AIRLINES serves directly forty-six cities in twenty
states and offers air and air-rail connections to scores of other
points. Its lines, in addition to linking the Atlantic and
the Pacific seaboards, connect the Great Lakes area to the Southwest,
the Pacific Northwest to the Rocky Mountain region and provide
the only through service on the Pacific Coast.
mountainous terrain. Included in the personnel are seven pilots,
each of whom has flown a million miles.
United Air Lines has a
pilot personnel of 150. Their first consideration is your safety and
comfort.
25,000,000 Miles NIGHT Flying Experience
United Air Lines is the only air line in the world with over 50 million
miles flying experience of which more than 25 million miles has been
flown at night. Over the routes where subsidiaries inaugurated air-
mail, express and passenger service six years ago, United Air Lines
now operates a fleet of 100 Boeing and Ford planes 37,500 miles
a day, or 13,500,000 miles annually, over 6,378 miles of Government
improved and lighted airways.
Four Experts Aground For Every Pilot Aloft
With United Air Lines, travel by air is much more than just a plane
in the sky. Back of the millions of dollars invested in transport
planes, modern hangar-depots, servicing plants and extensive ground
facilities, is a highly skilled operating and executive personnel (a
ground staff of 600). There are four experts on the ground for
All Proved Aids to Air Navigation Employed
All proved aids to aerial navigation are employed, including two-
Wasp and Hornet Engines
The latest features of aeronautical design and construction suggested
by millions of miles of regular schedule flying are incorporated in
United's fleet of passenger planes, all of which are powered with
the reliable Pratt & Whitney "Wasp" and "Hornet" engines.
way voice radio communication system. This airplane radio-telephone
equipment not only permits communication between pilots and ground
stations and other planes in flight, but also reception of U.S. Depart-
ment of Commerce directive radio beam signals. Pilots also have
the benefit of the extensive and complete airways weather reporting
service provided by trained meteorologists of the United States
Veteran Passenger and Mail Pilots
Weather Bureau and broadcast hourly by the Aeronautics Branch
of the Department of Commerce.
United's veteran passenger and mail pilots, whose average experience
is more than 20 times the flying experience required by the Govern-
ment for transport pilots, are generally recognized as being on a par
with any group of commercial flyers in the world. They are thoroughly
experienced transport pilots, accustomed to all variations of flying
conditions-night or day, winter or summer, at sea level or over
Fly With United Air Lines
Based on the firm foundation of six years' experience and 50,000,000
miles of air transport operations, United Air Lines invites you to
travel on its nation-wide air passenger, mail and express service.
